candidates.doc:
executeGainControlEffect implements the "gain_control" v2 primitive: "Gain
control of target creature[ an opponent controls][ until end of turn][.
Untap it/that creature.][ It/That creature gains KEYWORD(s) until end of
turn.]" (task-1998, verb_unmapped:gain_control). Indefinite by default;
effectValue["until_eot"]==true reverts control to the pre-steal controller
at the next cleanup step. The optional untap/keywords riders are bundled
into THIS atom's value rather than riding their own sequence atoms: the
v2 sequence-atom Target-routing (cards/converter.go's exactly-one-
targeted-atom cast stub, game/effect_sequence.go's routeSeqTargets) only
cleanly threads a resolved target to a SECOND atom by duplicating the
Target dict onto it, which either breaks the cast-time target requirement
(converter.go only builds the stub when exactly one atom carries Target)
or, left untargeted, falls through grant_keywords_until_eot's
affects_filter default and grants the keyword to the resolving spell/
ability object instead of the stolen creature. Not reused from
cardfns.GainControlUntilEOT (cardfns/lib_gain_control_until_eot.go) —
this package can't import cardfns — but mirrors its snapshot/steal/
EventCleanup-revert skeleton.

puts any matching triggered abilities on the stack. Use this instead of
calling Player.GainLife directly whenever GameState is available. The event
reports the amount actually applied — after any LifeGainModifier
replacement effect (Bilbo-class: "if you would gain life, you gain that
much life plus 1 instead") — not the pre-replacement amount, since Rule
603.4 triggers observe the game state after replacement effects apply.

the spell pre-effect, cardfns direct gains) routes through here so batch

own guard, mirrored here so no event fires for an empty gain).
